name: Monomark Engineering (India)
summary: Monomark Engineering, based in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, provides industrial operations and maintenance, metal fabrication and project execution for metals, cement, ports and engineering clients. Revenue grew from ₹390 cr in FY24 to ₹562 cr in FY26, and profit rose 42% in FY26 to ₹25.9 cr, though operating cash flow was only ₹8.1 cr. The issue is a fresh issue of 2.70 crore shares with no offer for sale, and ₹120 cr of it is earmarked for working capital, not new capacity. Customer concentration is very high: the top 10 customers gave 91% of FY26 revenue and Hindustan Zinc alone 35%; the price band is not yet announced.

fh1.finding: Revenue rose from ₹389.9 cr (FY24) to ₹561.9 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 20.1%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹389.9 cr, ₹475.0 cr, ₹561.9 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.77 at June 30, 2026 (borrowings ₹92.1 cr vs net worth ₹119.3 cr).

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose 9% (₹80.2 cr to ₹87.3 cr) while revenue rose 44% over FY24–FY26.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹60.1 cr, ₹73.3 cr, ₹116.7 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was ₹8.1 cr in FY26, about 31% of the ₹25.9 cr profit.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew 42.2% in FY26, from ₹18.2 cr to ₹25.9 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from 3.80% (FY24) to 3.83% (FY25) and 4.61% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on equity was 27.27% in FY26 (RoNW 22.19%).

pr5.finding: Peer margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: The price band is not announced, so the post-issue P/E cannot be computed (peer median P/E is about 31.5x).

va2.finding: The price band is not announced, so the post-issue price to book cannot be computed.

va3.finding: The price band is not announced, so the post-issue market cap to sales cannot be computed.

va4.finding: The price band is not announced; the last reported private allotment was in July 2025 at ₹38 a share.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 65.69% after the issue, down from 91.37%.

pg2.finding: The offer document states none of the promoters' shares are pledged.

pg3.finding: FY26 related-party payments (promoter pay ₹2.67 cr plus about ₹1.3 cr of equipment, rent and reimbursements to a promoter firm) are under 1% of revenue.

pg4.finding: Tax proceedings of ₹13.1 lakh are pending against the promoters.

is1.finding: The entire issue of 2.70 crore shares is fresh; there is no offer for sale.

is2.finding: The 2.70 crore new shares are about 28.1% of the 9.60 crore post-issue shares.

is3.finding: No selling shareholders, because there is no offer for sale.

up1.finding: Nothing funds capex, expansion or acquisitions; ₹120 cr goes to working capital and the rest to general corporate purposes.

up2.finding: None of the fresh issue goes to repaying debt.

up3.finding: The general corporate purposes amount is not disclosed (capped at 25%), as the issue size isn't fixed yet.

up4.finding: No proceeds go to repaying loans, so none repay promoter entities.

lg1.finding: Tax proceedings against the company total ₹1.20 cr, about 1% of the ₹116.7 cr net worth.

lg2.finding: An independent director faces a ₹20 lakh cheque-dishonour complaint and a separate criminal matter.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities are ₹56.5 cr, about 47.3% of net worth.

rk1.finding: The top 10 customers gave 91.2% of FY26 revenue, and Hindustan Zinc alone 35.4%.

rk2.finding: Supplier concentration figures were not found in public sources.

rk3.finding: Incorporated in September 2005, so about 21 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
